Capoeira is an exciting and dynamic Afro-Brazilian art-form that combines elements of movement, dance, martial arts, music, and game-play. Developed by African slaves and their descendants in Brazil, capoeira has a rich history and this beautiful art has survived through hundreds of years of exploitation and adversity. In 2014 capoeira was granted ‘Cultural Heritage Status’ by UNESCO the UN’s cultural arm.
As well as being an amazingly rewarding and fun activity, the practice of Capoeira develops excellent fitness, flexibility, mobility, coordination and balance.
It also enhances teamwork, communication, social skills and teaches mutual respect through its focus on working together and creating dialogues through movement. Capoeira also develops rhythm and musicality, and exposes capoeiristas to a foreign language and culture without even realizing it.
Hailing from Minas Gerais, Brazil, Capoeira Manchester is led by Contra Mestre Rander under the guidance of world-wide renowned master, Mestre Papa-Léguas. Training since childhood, Rander has dedicated a lifetime to developing and sharing capoeira in Brazil and overseas, only becoming more passionate about the art form as time passes. He firmly believes in the transformative power of capoeira and how it can significantly enrich people's lives.
There are NO REQUIREMENTS to start Capoeira, only willingness to learn and have fun.
What is capoeira?
- A non-contact Brazilian martial art
- Suitable for all ages and abilities
- Involves dance, gam-play, gymnastics and self-expression
- Based on group and pair work.
What can capoeira offer children?
- Physical health and fitness.
- Self-esteem and confidence
- Focus and concentration
- Respect
- Fun and friendship
